h1: Lampam Resort Phatthalung — a Lampam Beach resort just steps from the lakeshore
intro: If you want to wake up to the breeze off Songkhla Lake at Lampam Beach without a long drive, Lampam Resort is one of the closest places to the water in Phatthalung. It's a 3-star resort on Aphai Borirak Road in the Lampam area, about a 3-minute walk to Lampam Beach on the lakeshore. Its 68 air-conditioned rooms come with private balconies, and there's an on-site restaurant serving all three meals. The overall score is 8.0 from real guest reviews (Trip.com), and it's good value from around THB 700/night.

body.html: Lampam Beach is a popular spot on the Phatthalung shore of Songkhla Lake — locals come to catch the breeze, watch the sunrise and find fresh seafood. Lampam Resort's biggest strength is its location: it sits very close to Lampam Beach, about a 3-minute walk to the water. It suits travellers who want an easy lakeside feel more than a downtown base, with the local restaurants and souvenir shops of Lampam within walking distance.

There are 68 air-conditioned rooms, each with a private balcony, a fridge and a TV. Choices range from Standard Queen and Standard Twin rooms of about 25 sqm to a Family Room and a Dormitory for groups or budget travellers. Many reviews note the rooms feel more spacious than expected for the price, and the grounds are leafy with a garden. This is a place that leans on value and a lakeside setting rather than luxury.
"Affordable, spacious rooms, breakfast included, and Lampam Beach is a very short walk away. Lovely views, kind staff — a great spot for a relaxed lakeside stay."

The most frequent praise goes to its lakeside location, the good value and the friendly staff. There's an on-site restaurant serving breakfast, lunch and dinner, and many guests say the food is tasty and convenient — no need to head out. Common areas include a garden, a 24-hour reception, a lift, free parking and free Wi-Fi. It suits families, groups of friends and anyone in town for a sports event or function in the Lampam area who wants to stay close by.

To be honest, cleanliness and room condition are inconsistent. Some reviews mention dust, cobwebs in corners, worn furnishings and minimal toiletries, and a few note the tap water running yellow at times. This is why the cleanliness score sits around 7.5 while location and service rate higher. If you expect a crisp, brand-new room like a city hotel, set your expectations accordingly first.

Another thing to know is that Lampam Resort focuses on its lakeside location and low price rather than resort-style facilities. There's no large pool or spa. Some reviews say the air conditioning in certain rooms isn't cold enough on very hot days — if that happens, ask staff to move you or take a look. Overall it remains good value for travellers who care more about being near Lampam Beach than about a flawless room.

In short, Lampam Resort is best for travellers who want to stay by Lampam Beach, close to the water, at an easy price, and who aren't too fussy about how new the room is. If you want a spotless room, a downtown location or full facilities, look at a city hotel in Phatthalung such as the Khuha Sawan area instead. But if your goal is to sit by the lake, watch the sunrise and walk to the beach, this fits the bill at a wallet-friendly rate.

A tip from following the reviews: ask to see the room at check-in, since condition varies, so you can pick a clean one with cold air conditioning. If you're travelling in a group on a budget, the Dormitory is great value. And don't miss a walk to Lampam Beach at dawn or in the evening — that's when the lakeside is at its prettiest.

Just accept that cleanliness and room condition are inconsistent, some furnishings are worn, and there are no resort-style luxury facilities.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — Lampam Resort Phatthalung

faq.q: Where is Lampam Resort in Phatthalung, and how close is Lampam Beach?
faq.a: It's at 88 Moo 6, Aphai Borirak Road, Lampam, Mueang Phatthalung, on the shore of Songkhla Lake — about a 3-minute walk to Lampam Beach, a popular viewpoint and sunrise spot. Phatthalung town and Khao Ok Thalu are around 15 minutes by car, and the railway station is about 18 minutes.

faq.q: How much does Lampam Resort cost, and what room types are there?
faq.a: Rates start from around THB 700/night for a Standard Queen of about 25 sqm. There's also a Standard Twin (~฿750), a Family Room (~฿1,100) and a Dormitory with six queen beds (~฿1,500). Prices vary by season, so compare a few platforms before booking.

faq.q: Does Lampam Resort have a pool, and do rooms have balconies?
faq.a: The resort has no swimming pool, but there's an on-site restaurant, a garden, a 24-hour reception and free parking. Every room is air-conditioned with a private balcony. The main draw is the lakeside location within walking distance of Lampam Beach.

faq.q: Who is Lampam Resort best for?
faq.a: It's ideal for travellers who want to stay by Lampam Beach, close to the water, at an easy price — families, groups of friends, or anyone in town for a sports event or function in the Lampam area. If you want a brand-new room, a downtown location or full facilities, choose a city hotel in Phatthalung instead.

faq.q: Anything to know before booking Lampam Resort?
faq.a: Cleanliness and room condition are inconsistent — some reviews note dust, cobwebs, worn furnishings and minimal toiletries. It's worth asking to see the room at check-in, and if the air conditioning isn't cold enough, ask staff for help. Overall it's still good value for travellers who prioritise the lakeside location over a brand-new room.
